note: Literature systematically shows pediatric biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function variants present with spasticity, pyramidal signs, and seizures, distinguishing them from CADASIL.

evidence.text: In a systematic analysis of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants, 26 patients with biallelic loss-of-function variants presented with a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periventricular white matter changes, contrasting with classic CADASIL phenotypes.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia.

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in NOTCH3 consistently manifest as an early-onset autosomal recessive leukodystrophy characterized by developmental delay, spasticity, and epilepsy.

source.title: A novel homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant in a Moroccan patient: expanding the spectrum beyond CADASIL
source.quote: Emerging evidence shows that biallelic loss-of-function variants, unlike the gain-of-function variants underlying CADASIL, define a distinct autosomal recessive leukodystrophy characterized by early-onset pyramidal signs, epilepsy, and white matter abnormalities
